sentences.text: The name Aralosaurus means "Aral Sea lizard" because the fossils were found near the Aral Sea, while the species name tuberiferus means "bearing a tuber" due to a sharp rise in the nasal bone in front of the eye sockets.
This herbivorous dinosaur is classified as a lambeosaurine hadrosaurid, a subgroup of duck-billed dinosaurs where the parent group for the genus is Lambeosaurinae.

The animal measured approximately 6 to 9 meters in length and possessed over 1,000 teeth arranged in 30 rows, with the rear part of its skull being wide to suggest large jaw muscles used to power its chewing apparatus.
It possessed over 1,000 teeth arranged in 30 rows, a complex dental battery that allowed it to chew hard branches.
The discovery of nests with eggs suggests that Aralosaurus lived in herds and had safe places to nest.
The genus Aralosaurus was named by Anatoly Rozhdestvensky in 1968 after a partial skull was discovered in 1957 near the Shakh-Shakh locality in central Kazakhstan.
Rozhdestvensky estimated the skull size at 65 cm and the total body length at 6.5 meters, noting that the fossil specimen was likely immature because its cranial sutures were not fused.
Its teeth allowed it to chew hard branches, a trait common in ornithopod dinosaurs but unusual for reptiles.

A posterior nasal fragment rises in front of the orbits, forming or participating in a hollow crest-like structure that surrounded part of the respiratory system, though the exact shape and size of the crest-like structure remain unknown.

Angiosperms made up 75% of the local flora, with the remainder consisting of conifers, ginkgos, and cycads, while the fossil site yielded a diverse fauna including fish, amphibians, turtles with carapaces up to 75 cm long, reptiles, birds, mammals, and various dinosaur species.
Aralosaurus lived in subtropical to tropical floodplain and estuarine environments.

Aralosaurus is considered the most primitive lambeosaurine and is grouped with Canardia in the clade Aralosaurini; recent phylogenetic analyses place Aralosaurus close to Canardia within Lambeosaurinae, forming the tribe Aralosaurini, rather than with Gryposaurus or Maiasaura, and it lived approximately 20 million years before its relative Canardia.

Aralosaurus lived approximately 83.6 million years ago during the Late Cretaceous period, specifically during the late Cretaceous period, approximately 75 million years ago in the Campanian stage, with the time range extending from the Santonian to the Campanian, between 85.7 and 72.2 million years ago.
